normalization_or_editorial_flags.issue: French future arriverez-vous and English present 'do you arrive tomorrow' are compatible in context but not tense-identical; consider aligning for standalone drills.
Conversational subject-verb word order is valid spoken French but mixed with formal inversion; define whether the workbook intentionally teaches both registers.
French vouloir is more direct than English 'would you like'; align politeness/register if exact equivalence is the goal.
French specifies ce matin while English says today; not contradictory for breakfast, but standalone time precision differs.
Où avons-nous besoin d'aller ? is understandable but calqued; Où devons-nous aller ? is more idiomatic standard French.
requérir is grammatical but formal/legal in everyday contexts; need is better rendered by avoir besoin de for a general learner workbook.
je vous/te prie constructions are formal or dated relative to surrounding conversational material; native editorial review should normalize register.
French says 'tell me what I can do to help'; English says 'tell me how I can help'. Semantically close but not literal; either English can be tightened or pair replaced.
Adverb placement/comma usage is awkward for contemporary learner French; prefer Pouvez-vous me redire votre nom ? or Pouvez-vous me dire votre nom à nouveau ?.
Subjunctive veuille after fait penser is marked; native editorial review should choose a contemporary mood/register policy.
